hypothesis: With 256 threads per block and an items_per_block tile of 512, a grid-stride loop assigns up to two targets to each thread for larger inputs. Fewer threads and CTAs may reduce scheduling overhead, though the additional sequential target work per thread could instead hurt throughput. The pairwise arithmetic order and single-kernel interface remain unchanged; the controller must measure correctness and the prescribed geometric mean.
notes: This candidate is unmeasured. The prior 128/128 experiment was valid but slower than baseline; that result motivates testing a distinct larger item tile, not a claim that this candidate will be faster. The grid-stride index covers tails and remains complete when the launch tile differs from the block size, assuming positive launch dimensions.
transformations: Changed src/launch.json to use block=256, items_per_block=512, and no shared memory.
Changed target assignment to a grid-stride loop using a wide index so all outputs, including tails, are covered when the launch tile and block size differ.
Kept the pairwise force arithmetic and its iteration order unchanged; with the proposed tile, a thread may process two targets sequentially.
